subject: Post-demo follow-up: unit economics & service split confirmation
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@nimbusai.com>, CloudOps <ops@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: unit economics & service split confirmation

Samir / team — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap with the numbers we discussed so we have alignment before I circle back with pricing options. Attachment: Nimbus-Redwood-pricing-deck.pdf and token-econ-models.xlsx.

Key inputs from discovery (your confirmation needed):
- Expected steady-state volume: 6–12M tokens / month (peak bursts up to 20M).
- Budget guidance shared on call: target monthly spend roughly in the $8k–$16k range (you said "flexible depending on quality").
- Primary workloads: chat-driven customer support flows (sessioned, multi-turn), embeddings for semantic search + reranking for top-N results.

Proposed per-model split (initial recommendation):
- Chat (reply generation, multi-turn): 70% of tokens
- Embeddings (indexing/querying): 25% of tokens
- Rerank (re-scoring top candidates): 5% of tokens

Unit-econ targets (blended and per-model; target $/1M tokens):
- Blended target: $1,300 / 1M tokens (goal to hit or beat with routing/quantization)
- Chat (performance-first): $1,500 / 1M tokens (can be lowered to ~$1,100 with quantized variants)
- Embeddings: $850 / 1M tokens (embeddings-heavy workloads can drop to ~$600 with smaller embed models and caching)
- Rerank: $4,200 / 1M tokens (small portion of traffic; high compute but low volume)

Two recommended routing profiles (we can A/B):
1) Cost-optimized: route less latency-sensitive chat to redwood-chat-quant (q4_1) and serve embeddings on redwood-embed-small -> expected blended ~$1,050/1M.
2) Performance-first: most chat on redwood-chat-medium; embeddings on redwood-embed-48k -> expected blended ~$1,450/1M.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm the 6–12M tokens/month range and whether the 70/25/5 split looks right for your traffic?
- Do you have a strict target $/1M we should engineer toward (I heard a preference for sub-$1,200 if possible)?
- Any compliance gating (SOC2 evidence, IP/sharing rules) we should attach to the procurement docs?

If you confirm volumes + target $/1M, I’ll send a 3-option commercial sheet (self-serve hosted, reserved monthly commit, and a 12-month enterprise commit with pricing/discount bands) along with a recommended canary split for rollout.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call tomorrow if that’s easier.

—
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: Nimbus-Redwood-pricing-deck.pdf (25 pages), token-econ-models.xlsx (scenario tabs)

From: Samir Gupta <samir@nimbusai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: unit economics & service split confirmation

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Volume: the 6–12M range is accurate for months 1–3 of production. We expect growth to ~25M by month 6. For commercial planning, please price both the initial steady-state and a 6-month growth scenario.

2) Budget / $/1M: our internal procurement target is closer to $1,100 / 1M blended. We recognize that rerank is expensive — happy to reduce rerank volume by pre-filtering if that materially lowers cost.

3) Model mix: we want to lean toward cheaper embedding variants if we can keep semantic quality (tradeoff acceptable). For chat, sub-second p95 latency for agent responses is important for support SLA. If you can propose a hybrid where 60% of chat is routed to a cheaper quantized model and 40% to the higher-fidelity model for latency-sensitive flows, that would be ideal.

4) Compliance: SOC2 Type II is required; a redacted evidence bundle would speed procurement. Also need data retention policies and KMS integration notes.

If you can send (a) a two-scenario pricing table (initial / growth), (b) proposed canary split for rollout, and (c) SOC2 artifact pointer, we can take to procurement next week.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus AI
samir@nimbusai.com | +1 (212) 555-0114

Forwarding Samir's reply — they pushed for a blended target of ~$1,100/1M and expect growth to ~25M by month 6. Procurement will want SOC2 artifacts and KMS notes.

Suggested internal ask:
- Can we present three commercial scenarios (numbers are placeholders until pricing team confirms):
  A) Self-serve hosted (no commit) — blended $1,450/1M initial; growth pricing tiers at 15% off after 20M/mo.
  B) Reserved monthly commit (6–12M) — blended $1,200/1M with a 10% discount at 12-month prepay.
  C) Enterprise 12-month commit ($120k+) — blended $950–1,050/1M depending on commit level + SOC2 + priority support.

- Technical rollout (proposed canary): start with 60% chat -> redwood-chat-quant, 30% chat -> redwood-chat-medium (latency SLO paths), embeddings on redwood-embed-small with cache TTLs, rerank minimized to 3% for initial canary.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Monica: can you produce a two-scenario pricing table (initial 6–12M & growth 25M) and confirm whether we can hit a $950–1,050 blended band at $120k commit? ETA EOD Monday.
- Lauren: procurement contact — can you package SOC2 redacted bundle + KMS integration notes and route to Samir? ETA Tue morning.
- Alex: I’ll draft the three-option commercial and call out the rollout canary so we can share with Samir.

Notes on discount levers: committed spend, 12-month prepay, routing (embedding reductions), and feature gating (rerank on only high-confidence queries).

—
Alex

Will sync Monday am and I’ll prepare a single sheet to send to Samir after we align.

—Lauren
